title: The white elephant problem
text: Hosting the Olympics was once the pride of cities; now it is a {{1}} few of them queue for. The pattern repeats with grim {{2}}: a winning bid promising regeneration, a budget that {{3}} during construction, and gleaming venues that struggle to find a purpose once the Games close. Athens 2004 left a softball stadium {{4}} with weeds; Montreal needed thirty years to pay off 1976; Beijing's Bird's Nest survives largely as a tourist {{5}}. Economics explains the arithmetic: broadcast money flows to the International Olympic Committee, while {{6}} fall on the host, and cost estimates — already optimistic — {{7}} to rise once ground is broken. The reaction has been {{8}}: cities have withdrawn bids after referendums, and the committee now offers to spread events across several countries and existing venues rather than demand new stadiums. The Games survive; the era of every city building its own colossus may not.

gaps.explanation: 'now it is a prize few of them queue for' — something desirable; a price, penalty or burden is not something cities would queue for.
'repeats with grim predictability' — it can be foreseen every time; probability = likelihood.
'a budget that escalates during construction' — climbs steeply; erode = wear away gradually.
'a stadium overgrown with weeds' — 'overgrown with' is the fixed collocation; overtake = catch up and pass.
'survives as a tourist attraction' — the standard term; attribute = a quality, auction = a public sale.
'broadcast money flows to the IOC, while costs fall on the host' — the expenses; costumes and trophies are not financial burdens, and revenues would flow in, not fall on.
'estimates proceed to rise' — continue and then; 'precede' means come before, the classic confusable.
'the reaction has been swift' — fast; sift = put through a sieve, shrill = high and piercing.
